main_text.l: Opponitúrne quies quieti,sicut
motus motui?
Imò, quando videlicet sunt in contrarijs termi-
nis. Quies enim rursus eadem ratione invenitur op-
posita quieti,qua motus sunt oppositi sibi invicem.
Quinetiam sicut motus secundū locum alius est na-
turalis,alius violentus, & hi sibi invicem adversan-
tur: ita quies quoq; alia est naturalis,alia violenta,
& altera alteri adversatur.
Est'ne quies contraria mutationi,
perinde ac motui?
Nihil prohibet, quatenus in ipsis mutationibus
occurrit contrarietas,eatenus etiam in quiete inve-
niri ex altera parte contrarietatem. Etenim specta-
tur contrarietas in mutationibus prorsus quemad-
modum in motibus. ut enim est motus alius natura-
lis,alius violentus: ita mutatio quoque alia natura-
lis est,alia violenta. Ex quo fit,ut corruptio natu-
ralis contraria sit corruptioni violentæ, & gene-
rationi naturali generatio violenta. Est autem ge-
neratio violeta, veluti si quis flores vel ramos faciat
crescere subitò, vel alio tempore, vel aliter quàm se-
cundum naturā crescere solent. Similiter iudicandū
de augmento & decremeto,itemq; de alteratione.

page.notes: The printed page is not cut off at the foot; the paragraph continues on the next page after the catchword "alter". "violeta" in the line "Est autem generatio violeta" appears to be a printing error for "violenta"; left as printed. A printed asterisk after "contrarius" in the heading "Est'ne motus sursum tendens contrarius*" is a printer's mark and is omitted. The "u" in "Quies" and the underline-like mark over "Q" and "Quinetiam" are type marks, not letters; they are not transcribed. The page number "115" at top right is slightly worn; read as 115. The first line "Imò" has the italic word "Imò" printed in italics; rendered as italic.
